# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 exporting manufacturers). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| supplier_diversity | Number of distinct input suppliers (standardized), 2021-2022 |
| export_growth_2023 | Export value growth in 2023 (percent index) |
| log_sales_2020 | Log sales, 2020 |
| years_exporting_2020 | Years since first export, standardized, 2020 |
| export_growth_2020 | Export value growth in 2020, standardized |
| buyer_rating_2023 | Average rating from foreign buyers, 2023 |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| product_group | Sector: durables / nondurables |
| inventory_days_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |

| certified_iso | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| debt_ratio_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of supplier diversification on export growth?

Approach: OLS of export_growth_2023 on supplier_diversity with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I focus on the north region subsample, where the data are most comparable, control for firm size, firm age and the pre-period value of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on supplier_diversity is 0.316 (SE 0.353, p = 0.3708, N = 634).

Conclusion: no effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
df = df[df['region'] == 'north']
y = df["export_growth_2023"]
lo, hi = y.quantile([0.01, 0.99])
df = df[(y >= lo) & (y <= hi)]
X = sm.add_constant(df[['supplier_diversity', 'log_sales_2020', 'years_exporting_2020', 'export_growth_2020']].astype(float))
fit = sm.OLS(df["export_growth_2023"].values, X.values).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print("n =", len(df))
print("coef =", fit.params[1], "se =", fit.bse[1], "p =", fit.pvalues[1])

content.text:
I rejected the report. I wrote `verdict.json` with the decision "reject".

The "no effect" conclusion depends on the analyst restricting the sample to the north region, with no real justification. I re-ran the regression with the same controls (firm size, years exporting, prior export growth) on other samples. The estimates for supplier diversity were:

| Sample | N | Coefficient | SE | p-value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All regions | 2000 | 0.69 | 0.24 | 0.004 |
| North | 648 | 0.34 | 0.37 | 0.35 |
| Central | 678 | 0.63 | 0.44 | 0.16 |
| South | 674 | 1.11 | 0.43 | 0.01 |

The north is the weakest of the three regions, and the full sample and the south both show a positive, statistically significant effect. A null result from a hand-picked subgroup is mostly a power problem, so it doesn't show the effect is absent. Adding the remaining firm characteristics as controls barely changes any of these numbers.

The report's figures for the north (0.316, SE 0.353, N = 634) are consistent with `analysis.py`. My north estimate differs slightly because I did not trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.
